chapter: Clubs, readers and musicians he knew
title: Reading music and carrying orchestrations to jobs
summary: He was not a sight-reader but learned parts between tunes, and always brought orchestrations to jobs.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Would you say that your moods would play with reading bands then, in other words? Huh? Since you were mostly a reading musician, did you play mostly with bands that had orchestrations and things like that?

Well, no. Most all the bands you played with, there was more people who didn't read than with Red. There was only a few with Red, you know. And then with Red wasn't professional readers because I was one of them. You were? Oh, I wasn't professional. I couldn't read on site. You know, somebody gave me a sheet and said, play this. Couldn't do that. But you had to start. I didn't go over it. Plenty of times that happened to me on the job. The fellas say, I got a piece of music I'd like for you to play. Now you got it? Say, yeah, let me see it. Well they let me see it. What I'd do is sit it on the side and in between tunes I would mute the trumpet and run over it. And then after I was able to run over it, me being the leader of the band, the balance of the band would be able to play. Because them wouldn't, wasn't making the right note, they'd be harmonized anyhow, so they played right on.
Had plenty of that. Did you, did you often play with bands, like, I'm not talking about bands, but regular bands that had more than one trumpet?
No, the only ones I played with that had more than one trumpet was these street bands.
I see. In your time they didn't have many really big bands.
No, six piece bands, five piece bands, they would use. No one was always a small piece. Yeah, they were small, six piece, sometimes seven pieces.
You know, it would run between five and seven. In other words you wouldn't use orchestration for the whole band, you would only use music for you.

Well I had the whole orchestration all the time, because I couldn't tell when somebody might ask, they wouldn't use it, you know, somebody, you hire a band, plenty of times you hire people, you don't know what they can do. Right. Until they get on the job. And then they'd say, well, some of you pass on the orchestration, the part, and they'd say, well, I don't use it. Some wouldn't say nothing, they'd try to fool you. And they couldn't fool you if you knew. You know, they'd sit there and, they could do so well without it, so they'd sit there and do something, you know, try to fool you and make you really a thing. But you would always bring music with you. Oh, all the time. All the time. And sometimes you would. I brought music all the time. Even if I went on an advertisement where you wouldn't need but three or four tunes to play advertising, I brought orchestration with me all the time. In other words I had a habit of, it was customary for me to bring my music with me. Because I didn't know.
That was orchestration that you brought?
Yeah, yeah, orchestration. Do you still have some of that music? No, I don't have a bit of it.
